title: Role boundaries and SIEM evidence playbook
content:
Summary:
This playbook proposes a role-bounded RBAC v2 design focused on clear separation of duties, machine-friendly audit events, and automated evidence exports to our SIEM. It is intended as a pragmatic migration guide for teams owning product routes and infra, with example audit schemas, mapping tables, and a staged rollout plan.

Design principles (short):
- Minimal privilege by default: roles grant narrow capabilities; escalation paths explicit and auditable.
- Resource-centric scoping: permissions attach to resource types (model, deployment, project, route) + resource id where needed.
- Deterministic mapping: human-readable role names map to a canonical permission set for automation and evidence collection.
- Audit-first: every role decision that affects production control surfaces must emit structured evidence.
- Backwards compatible fallbacks: existing tokens & routes continue to work during migration; compatibility layer for older services.

Role-bound contexts (examples):
1) Platform-admin: global infra operations (cluster/pools, capacity quotas, billing actions). Should be limited to SRE and infra leads.
2) Model-onboard: ability to add/approve new model artifacts to catalog; tied to model namespace.
3) Deployment-operator: create/update dedicated/private deployments; scoped to project or customer-customer-id.
4) Route-owner: manage Redwood API routes, rollouts, fallbacks — scoped to route-id.
5) Read-only-auditor: view-only access to audit logs and usage dashboards (no token creation).

Permissions model proposal (compact):
- Permission tokens are triple (action, resource_type, scope) where scope is one of {global, org, project, resource}.
- Example granular actions: read, write, deploy, approve, rotate-keys, export-logs.
- Roles are bundles of permission tokens plus metadata (owner, TTL for sudo-like grants, review cadence).
- Role inheritance: discouraged except for explicit composed roles (e.g., "model-onboard+route-owner") with clear ownership.

Audit/event schema (machine-first):
- All audit events should be single-line JSON records emitted to the central logging pipeline. Primary fields (required):
  - event_id (string UUID)
  - timestamp (RFC3339)
  - actor_id (string, canonical: "user:<id>" or "service:<id>")
  - actor_roles (list of role ids active for actor at time of action)
  - action (string, canonical verb like "route.create", "model.publish", "key.rotate")
  - resource_type (string)
  - resource_id (string|null)
  - outcome (enum: success|failure|unauthorized|error)
  - reason (string, optional short human message)
  - evidence_refs (list of URIs pointing to captured evidence: signed-policy, config-diff, approver-ticket)
  - request_context (map-like string: e.g., "ip=1.2.3.4;region=us-west-2;seq=12345") - stringified to avoid nested JSON in older sinks

Note: some fields (request_context) are intentionally stringified for compatibility with legacy SIEM ingestion paths; downstream parsers can split the K/V pairs.

Audit JSON example (single-line):
{"event_id":"evt-9a7b3c","timestamp":"2025-01-24T16:12:32Z","actor_id":"user:234","actor_roles":["route-owner:team-nimbus"],"action":"route.update","resource_type":"route","resource_id":"route:public-completions","outcome":"success","reason":"updated timeout and batching","evidence_refs":["s3://rbw-evidence/prod/route-update/evt-9a7b3c.json"],"request_context":"ip=34.82.12.8;region=us-west-2;seq=65432"}

Evidence automation patterns:
- Trigger points to capture evidence: role grant/revoke, route rollout change, model publish, private deployment creation, key rotations.
- Evidence bundle content: signed role Delta (who changed which roles), config snapshot (deployment spec), canary evaluation summary (if applicable), approval ticket id, and TTL for retention.
- Storage: evidence bundles are stored in a protected S3 prefix with object ACLs keyed by event_id and immutability flag (WORM) for retention requirements.
- Automation flow (high-level):
  1) Action occurs; RBAC service emits audit event + local staged evidence bundle.
  2) Evidence bundler validates and pushes to S3, returns evidence URI(s).
  3) Audit event augmented with evidence_refs and forwarded to logging -> SIEM.
  4) SIEM content rules correlate event_id with evidence URI and generate alerts or retain for compliance search.

SIEM export and mapping notes:
- Primary export format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Export job pushes to SIEM via HTTPS bulk ingest or to intermediate Kafka topic (preferred for buffering).
- Field mappings for SIEM (recommended):
  - event_id -> rbw.event_id
  - timestamp -> @timestamp
  - actor_id -> rbw.actor.id
  - actor_roles -> rbw.actor.roles (array)
  - action -> rbw.action
  - resource_type/resource_id -> rbw.resource.type / rbw.resource.id
  - outcome -> rbw.outcome
  - evidence_refs -> rbw.evidence.uris
  - request_context -> rbw.request.context (string)
- If SIEM enforces a schema (ELK/Datadog), create an ingest-time pipeline that extracts request_context KV pairs and indexes them as rbw.request.ip, rbw.request.region, etc.

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - prep (2 weeks):
- Inventory existing roles and tokens (linear export script: TODO link JIRA-SEC-872).
- Draft canonical role catalog and map to product owners for review.
- Build compatibility shim spec for legacy tokens.

Phase 1 - pilot (4 weeks):
- Select two teams (Console + Dedicated infra) as pilots.
- Deploy RBAC v2 service behind feature flag.
- Enable full evidence bundling for pilot actions; verify evidence push and SIEM indexing (use test SIEM index).
- Collect pain points and log volume metrics.

Phase 2 - increment (6–8 weeks):
- Ramp to org-level: onboard remaining core product teams.
- Enable role templating and automated periodic reviews (90-day review).
- Add ingest-time SIEM pipelines to parse request_context and evidence_refs.

Phase 3 - org-wide enforcement (2–4 weeks):
- Turn on enforcement for new role grants; continue read-only compatibility mode for legacy tokens for 60 days.
- Start retention WORM policies on evidence S3 prefixes.

Rollout checklist (quick):
- [ ] Export current role & permission matrix
- [ ] Review canonical role catalog with product owners
- [ ] Implement audit schema emitters in gateway and RBAC service
- [ ] Evidence bundler: S3 + immutability + signed upload
- [ ] SIEM ingest pipeline + mapping tests
- [ ] Pilot teams onboarded + retro
- [ ] Public runbook for on-call + incident playbooks updated

Operational considerations:
- Log volume: sample rate for verbose fields (config diffs) to control cost. Full evidence bundles stored in S3; SIEM keeps references only.
- PII: scrub sensitive user input before bundling (mask keys, tokens).
- Latency: evidence upload is asynchronous; do not block user-facing flows. Failures to push evidence should produce a high-severity ticket but not prevent the action (unless action is compliance-blocked).
- Backup & retention: default evidence TTL = 365 days; customer-specific retention may override.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we enforce role inheritance at all, or require explicit aggregation? (product owners to decide; recommended: explicit aggregation)
- Should evidence bundles be signed with customer-managed keys for private deployments? (pro: stronger auditability; con: operational complexity)
- What is the canonical actor identity format for CI/service accounts vs user sessions? propose: "user:<id>", "service:<id>", "token:<id>".

Next steps (owner: Sasha Kim):
- Week 1: run role inventory script and publish CSV to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-SEC/Role-Model-V2).
- Week 2: prototype audit emitter changes in gateway (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2/pull/84).
- Schedule pilot kickoff with Console and Dedicated infra (email thread: #sec-rbac-migration).

Notes to self / draft comments: 
- Keep this doc lightweight; move canonical role table to Confluence page and link from this playbook.
- Expect 1–2 followups: SIEM field name normalization and evidence retention SLAs.

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC/Role-Model-V2
- JIRA epic: JIRA-SEC-872 (rbac v2 rollout)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2/pull/84
